posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: OpenAI Employee Arrested Over Hidden Recording Device. An OpenAI employee has been arrested and accused of planting a hidden recording device inside an executive conference room at the company’s San Francisco offices. Bloomberg’s Rachel Metz discusses the FBI investigation, how the inexpensive device was discovered and OpenAI’s response. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Modal CEO: AI Has Entered a ‘New Era of Software’. AI cloud startup Modal has raised $750 million at a $15.75 billion post-money valuation as demand surges for the infrastructure needed to build and run AI applications. CEO Erik Bernhardsson discusses the company’s more than 3 billion AI sandboxes, growing demand for inference and reinforcement learning, and why increasingly capable agents will need secure virtual environments where they can execute code and eventually take on longer-running tasks. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: AI Boom Drives ASML Higher as Nvidia Bets on Europe. Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down ASML's earnings after the company raised its sales forecast for 2026 and said it aims to increase production of its chip-making machines to keep up with soaring AI spending. Plus, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announces plans to invest an additional $2 billion in European deals. And, an inside look at the making of Grand Theft Auto VI, expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time. (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text: Alleged OpenAI spy vibe-coded a surveillance device using his wife's chatbot account. A Saudi national working as an engineer at OpenAI was arrested for allegedly planting an audio recording device, wrapped in toilet paper, inside the company's executive conference room. According to the indictment, he built the spy tool by vibe-coding it with a chatbot. If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison.
